original_ai_prompt: Design the network for a new retail branch. We have two POS terminals that must be isolated for compliance, a back-office PC, IP security cameras, and free guest WiFi for customers. POS and back office stay wired; guests are wireless. Cable internet on site.
cleaned_prompt: Design the network for a new retail branch. We have two POS terminals that must be isolated for compliance, a back-office PC, IP security cameras, and free guest WiFi for customers. POS and back office stay wired; guests are wireless. Cable internet on site.
expected_behaviour: REFUSE-BY-NAME: real IP security cameras cannot be expressed — the schema's only IoT kind is smart_led ('kind: Literal["smart_led"]'), and relabelling cameras as smart LEDs is exactly the mislabel the engine must not do. The correct output names the camera limitation and offers either the expressible smart-LED IoT device or an explicit statement that IP cameras are out of model scope. The POS/back-office/guest segmentation itself is buildable.

why_suitable: Retail/POS realism (PCI-style isolation) plus an honest capability-gap probe: cameras aren't a verified IoT kind. Prevents the model from pretending it can place real IP cameras.
